title.zh: 卷1 帝紀第1 文帝上
title.raw: 卷1 帝紀第1 文帝上 Volume 1 Annals 1: Emperor Wen 1

sentences.zh: 文帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, Part One
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Wen, Part One

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝姓宇文氏，諱泰，字黑獺，代武川人也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor Emperor Wen bore the surname Yuwen; his taboo name was Tai, his style name Heitai; he was a native of Wuchuan in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, canonically titled Grand Progenitor, was of the Yuwen clan; his given name Tai (taboo form), courtesy name Heitai; he came from Wuchuan in Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先出自炎帝神農氏，為黃帝所滅，子孫遯居朔野。

translations.literal: His ancestors traced back to the Flame Emperor Shennong; they were destroyed by the Yellow Emperor, and their descendants fled to dwell in the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The clan traced its descent to Shennong, the Flame Emperor. After the Yellow Emperor overthrew them, their line retreated into the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 有葛烏菟者，雄武多算略，鮮卑慕之，奉以為主，遂總十二部落，世為大人。

translations.literal: There was one Ge Wutu, bold in arms and rich in stratagems; the Xianbei admired him and made him their leader, whereupon he gathered the twelve tribes under his rule and for generations served as their paramount chief.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Wutu rose as a warrior of force and cunning whom the Xianbei chose as chief; he united twelve tribes, and his heirs held the title of paramount leader for generations.

sentences.zh: 其後曰普回，因狩得玉璽三紐，有文曰皇帝璽，普回心異之，以為天授。

translations.literal: Later came Puhui, who while hunting obtained a jade seal with three loops bearing the inscription "Imperial Seal"; Puhui marveled at it in his heart and took it as a mandate from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui, a later descendant, found while hunting a tripartite jade seal engraved "Imperial Seal"; taking it for Heaven's grant, he cherished it as a sign of destiny.

sentences.zh: 其俗謂天曰宇，謂君曰文，因號宇文國，幷以為氏焉。

translations.literal: In their custom they called Heaven "Yu" and a lord "Wen"; hence they styled their state the Yuwen State and also took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Their tongue called Heaven yu and ruler wen; from that came the name Yuwen for both their realm and their clan.

sentences.zh: 普回子莫𨚗，自陰山南徙，始居遼西，是曰獻侯，為魏舅生之國。

translations.literal: Puhui's son Moqi moved south from beyond the Yin Mountains and first settled in Liaoxi; he was called Marquis Xian and his domain was that of Wei Jiusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui's son Moqi migrated south from the Yin range into Liaoxi, took the title Marquis Xian, and ruled the territory later known as Wei Jiusheng's state.

sentences.zh: 九世至侯豆歸，為慕容晃所滅。

translations.literal: Nine generations on came Hou Dougui, who was destroyed by Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations later Hou Dougui's line was extinguished by Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 其子陵仕燕，拜駙馬都尉，封玄菟公。

translations.literal: His son Ling entered the service of Yan, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Son-in-Law, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Ling served the Yan court as commandant of the imperial son-in-law's horse guards and received the title Duke of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 魏道武將攻中山，陵從慕容寶禦之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu of Wei was about to attack Zhongshan, Ling followed Murong Bao to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: As Wei Emperor Daowu marched on Zhongshan, Ling joined Murong Bao in the defense.

sentences.zh: 寶敗，陵率甲騎五百歸魏，拜都牧主，賜爵安定侯。

translations.literal: Bao was defeated; Ling led five hundred armored horsemen back to Wei, was appointed Master of the Capital Pastures, and was granted the title Marquis of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao's defeat Ling brought five hundred armored riders to Wei, received appointment as master of the capital pastures, and the marquisate of Anding.

sentences.zh: 天興初，徙豪傑於代都，陵隨例遷武川焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, when worthy families were relocated to the capital at Dai, Ling was moved to Wuchuan according to the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Tianxing the court relocated leading families to the Dai capital; Ling's household was resettled to Wuchuan like the rest.

sentences.zh: 陵生系，系生韜，並以武略稱。

translations.literal: Ling begat Xi; Xi begat Tao; both were renowned for military prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's son was Xi, and Xi's son Tao; both won fame as men of arms.

sentences.zh: 韜生肱。

translations.literal: Tao begat Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's son was Gong.

sentences.zh: 肱任俠有氣幹。

translations.literal: Gong was a chivalrous man of forceful character.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was a man of bold spirit who lived by the code of the knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 正光末，沃野鎮人破六汗拔陵作亂，遠近多應之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengguang era, Poliuhan Balang of Woye garrison raised rebellion, and many from near and far joined him.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Zhengguang, Balang of the Poliuhan clan at Woye garrison revolted, drawing followers from across the region.

sentences.zh: 其偽署王衛可孤徒黨最盛，肱乃糾合鄉里斬可孤，其衆乃散。

translations.literal: Among the bandits of Wang Wei Kegu, whom the rebels had installed as king, his following was the strongest; Gong thereupon rallied the countryside and beheaded Kegu, and his host then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The strongest rebel band rallied around their puppet king Wei Kegu; Gong mustered local men, killed Kegu, and broke the force apart.

sentences.zh: 後避地中山，遂陷於鮮于修禮。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Zhongshan for safety and there fell into the hands of Xianyu Xiuli.
translations.idiomatic: He later took refuge at Zhongshan and ended up serving under Xianyu Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 修禮令肱還統其部衆。

translations.literal: Xiuli ordered Gong to return and take command of his tribal following.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuli sent Gong back to lead his original troops.

sentences.zh: 後為定州軍所破，歿於陣。

translations.literal: Later he was broken by the army of Ding Province and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was later cut down in battle by the Dingzhou forces.

sentences.zh: 武成初，追尊曰德皇帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he was posthumously honored as Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wucheng era he received the posthumous title Emperor De.

sentences.zh: 太祖，德皇帝之少子也。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke was the youngest son of Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was Emperor De's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰王氏，孕五月，夜夢抱子昇天，纔不至而止。

translations.literal: His mother was the lady Wang; she was pregnant five months when at night she dreamed of embracing her child and ascending to Heaven, stopping just short of reaching it.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wang, was five months pregnant when she dreamed she held her son and rose toward Heaven, halting just before the summit.

sentences.zh: 寤而告德皇帝，德皇帝喜曰：「雖不至天，貴亦極矣。

translations.literal: On waking she told Emperor De, and Emperor De said joyfully: "Though he did not reach Heaven, his nobility will be utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When she woke she told Emperor De, who said gladly: "He may not have reached Heaven, yet his eminence will be supreme.

sentences.zh: 」生而有黑氣如蓋，下覆其身。

translations.literal: " At birth there was a black vapor like a canopy covering him from above.
translations.idiomatic: " When he was born a black mist like a canopy descended over his body.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺，方顙廣額，美鬚髯，髮長委地，垂手過膝，背有黑子，宛轉若龍盤之形，面有紫光，人望而敬畏之。

translations.literal: When he grew up he stood eight chi in height, with a square forehead and broad brow, a handsome beard and whiskers; his hair hung to the ground, his hands reached below his knees; on his back was a black mark winding like a coiled dragon, and his face bore a violet glow—men who looked upon him felt awe and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Full grown he stood eight feet tall, square-browed and broad of forehead, with a fine beard and hair that swept the ground and arms that passed his knees. A dark birthmark on his back curled like a dragon; a violet light shone on his face, and those who saw him were struck with reverence.

sentences.zh: 少有大度，不事家人生業，輕財好施，以交結賢士大夫。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed great forbearance, did not attend to the family's livelihood, was light with wealth and generous in giving, and thereby formed ties with worthy gentlemen and officials.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was open-handed and magnanimous, cared little for household trade, lavished gifts freely, and won the friendship of learned men and officials.

sentences.zh: 少隨德皇帝在鮮于修禮軍。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Emperor De in Xianyu Xiuli's army.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served with Emperor De in the forces of Xianyu Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮殺修禮，太祖時年十八，榮遂任以將帥。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong killed Xiuli, the Grand Duke was then eighteen years old, and Rong thereupon entrusted him with command as a general.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong murdered Xiuli when Yuwen Tai was eighteen; Rong then put him in charge of troops as a field commander.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其無成，與諸兄謀欲逃避，計未行，會爾朱榮擒葛榮，定河北，太祖隨例遷晉陽。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke knew that Rong would accomplish nothing; he and his elder brothers plotted to flee, but before the plan could be carried out, Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong and pacified Hebei, and the Grand Duke was relocated to Jinyang according to the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai saw that Ge Rong was bound to fail and conspired with his brothers to escape. Before they could act, Erzhu Rong seized Ge Rong and secured Hebei; Yuwen Tai was then resettled to Jinyang like other captives.

sentences.zh: 榮以太祖兄弟雄傑，懼或異己，遂托以他罪，誅太祖第三兄洛生，復欲害太祖。

translations.literal: Rong, because the Grand Duke and his brothers were heroic figures, feared they might turn against him; he therefore framed them on other charges, executed the Grand Duke's third elder brother Luosheng, and again sought to kill the Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong feared the Yuwen brothers' prowess and moved against them on trumped-up charges: he executed Yuwen Tai's third brother Luosheng and tried to kill Yuwen Tai as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖自理家冤，辭旨慷慨，榮感而免之，益加敬待。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke pleaded his family's innocence on his own behalf, his words forceful and impassioned; Rong was moved and spared him, treating him with still greater respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai defended his clan in person with fierce eloquence; Erzhu Rong was impressed, spared him, and treated him with growing esteem.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，燕州亂，太祖始以統軍從榮征之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang, when Yan Province rebelled, the Grand Duke first took the field as army commander under Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang 2 (526), when Yanzhou rose in revolt, Yuwen Tai first campaigned as army commander under Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 先是，北海王顥奔梁，梁人立為魏主，令率兵入洛。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, had fled to Liang; the Liang installed him as ruler of Wei and ordered him to lead troops into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai, had defected to Liang; the southern court set him up as a rival Wei sovereign and sent him marching on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊帝出居河內以避之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei withdrew to Henei to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang left the capital for Henei to escape the invasion.

sentences.zh: 榮遣賀拔岳討顥，仍迎孝莊帝。

translations.literal: Rong dispatched Helba Yue to attack Hao and at the same time to welcome Emperor Xiaozhuang back.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong sent Helba Yue to defeat Hao and escort Emperor Xiaozhuang home.

sentences.zh: 太祖與岳有舊，乃以別將從岳。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke was old friends with Yue and therefore followed him as a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai and Helba Yue were already acquainted, so he joined the campaign as a detached commander under Yue.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊帝反正，以功封寧都子，邑三百戶，遷鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was restored to the throne, for his merit the Grand Duke was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ningdu with a fief of three hundred households, and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's restoration Yuwen Tai was enfeoffed as viscount of Ningdu with three hundred households, promoted to general who pacifies the distance, and made colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 万俟醜奴作亂關右，孝莊帝遣爾朱天光及岳等討之，太祖遂從岳入關，先鋒破偽行臺尉遲菩薩等。

translations.literal: Wan'niu Chounu raised rebellion in the Guanzhong region; Emperor Xiaozhuang dispatched Erzhu Tianguang together with Yue and others to suppress him, and the Grand Duke followed Yue into the passes, serving as vanguard and breaking the false Commissioner Yuchi Pusa and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan'niu Chounu rebelled in Guanzhong, Emperor Xiaozhuang sent Erzhu Tianguang and Helba Yue against him. Yuwen Tai entered the passes with Yue, led the van, and routed the puppet commissioner Yuchi Pusa.

sentences.zh: 及平醜奴，定隴右，太祖功居多，遷征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫，增邑三百戶，加直閣將軍，行原州事。

translations.literal: When Chounu was pacified and Longyou secured, the Grand Duke's merit was greatest; he was promoted to General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, his fief was increased by three hundred households, he was made general of the inner gate, and acted as governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Chounu's defeat and the pacification of Longyou, Yuwen Tai's service stood foremost. He was made general who conquers the west and grand master with the golden seal and purple ribbon, gained three hundred more households, received the title general of the inner gate, and governed Yuanzhou in commission.

sentences.zh: 時關隴寇亂，百姓凋殘，太祖撫以恩信，民皆悅服。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and rebels ravaged the Guanzhong and Longyou region, and the people were wasted and scattered; the Grand Duke treated them with kindness and good faith, and the people all rejoiced and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: With Guanzhong and Longyou torn by rebellion and the populace in ruins, Yuwen Tai won them over with clemency and trust until the people gladly obeyed.

sentences.zh: 咸喜曰：「早值宇文使君，吾等豈從逆亂。

translations.literal: They all said gladly: "Had we met Commissioner Yuwen sooner, we would never have followed rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people said with relief: "If only Commissioner Yuwen had come earlier—we would never have joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」太祖嘗從數騎於野，忽聞簫鼓之音，以問從人，皆云莫之聞也。

translations.literal: " Once the Grand Duke was riding in the open country with a few horsemen when he suddenly heard the sound of flutes and drums; he asked his attendants, but all said they heard nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Once, riding abroad with only a few companions, he suddenly heard flute and drum music; when he asked his escort, none of them heard a thing.

sentences.zh: 普泰二年，爾朱天光東拒齊神武，留弟顯壽鎮長安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putai, Erzhu Tianguang went east to oppose Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu, leaving his younger brother Xianshou to hold Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai 2 (530), Erzhu Tianguang marched east against Gao Huan (Qi Shenwu), leaving his brother Xianshou to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史侯莫陳悅為天光所召，將軍衆東下。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue, governor of Qin Province, was summoned by Tianguang and was about to lead his army east.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue, governor of Qinzhou, received Tianguang's summons and prepared to march east with his troops.

sentences.zh: 岳知天光必敗，欲留悅共圖顯壽，而計無所出。

translations.literal: Yue knew that Tianguang was certain to be defeated and wished to keep Yue with him to join in a plot against Xianshou, but could think of no means to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Helba Yue foresaw Tianguang's defeat and wanted Houmochen Yue to stay and help seize Xianshou, yet he could devise no plan.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂岳曰：「今天光尚邇，悅未有二心，若以此事告之，恐其驚懼，然悅雖為主將，不能制物，若先說其衆，必人有留心。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said to Yue: "Tianguang is still near, and Yue has not yet wavered in loyalty; if we disclose this matter to him, I fear he will be alarmed. Yet though Yue is the chief commander, he cannot control his men; if we first win over the troops, some among them are sure to hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai told Yue: "Tianguang is still close, and Houmochen Yue has not yet turned disloyal—tell him outright and he may panic. But though Yue commands the army, he cannot fully control it; speak first to the ranks and some will surely balk.

sentences.zh: 進失爾朱之期，退恐人情變動，乘•此說悅，事無不遂。

translations.literal: To advance would miss Erzhu's deadline; to retreat would risk a shift in sentiment. Seizing this moment, persuade Houmochen Yue, and the affair cannot fail.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on misses Erzhu's schedule; staying back risks unrest among the men. Seizing this moment to win Yue over, you cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」岳大喜，卽令太祖入悅軍說之，悅遂不行。

translations.literal: " Yue was greatly pleased and at once sent the Grand Duke into Houmochen Yue's camp to persuade him, and Houmochen Yue thereupon did not march.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was delighted and sent Yuwen Tai into Houmochen Yue's camp; persuaded, Yue stayed put.

sentences.zh: 乃相率襲長安，令太祖輕騎為前鋒。

translations.literal: They then joined forces in a surprise attack on Chang'an, with the Grand Duke leading the light cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: They then struck Chang'an together, with Yuwen Tai's light cavalry in the van.

sentences.zh: 太祖策顯壽怯懦，聞諸軍將至，必當東走，恐其遠遁，乃倍道兼行。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke calculated that Xianshou was cowardly; hearing that the armies were about to arrive, he would surely flee east, and fearing he might escape far away, he pressed on at double speed day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Xianshou a coward who would bolt east at the first rumor of attack, Yuwen Tai raced ahead day and night lest the man escape.

sentences.zh: 顯壽果已東走，追至華山，擒之。

translations.literal: Xianshou had indeed already fled east; they pursued him to Mount Hua and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianshou had already fled east; they overtook him at Mount Hua and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太昌元年，岳為關西大行臺，以太祖為左丞，領岳府司馬，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, Yue became Grand Commissioner of the Western Passes, appointing the Grand Duke as left director and chief marshal of Yue's headquarters, with the additional title of regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang 1 (531), Helba Yue was made grand commissioner of the western passes and named Yuwen Tai his left director and headquarters marshal, with the added rank of regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 事無巨細，皆委決焉。

translations.literal: Whether the matter was great or small, all were entrusted to his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Great or small, every affair went through him for final judgment.

sentences.zh: 齊神武旣破爾朱，遂專朝政。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu, having broken the Erzhu clan, then monopolized court power.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing the Erzhu faction, Gao Huan (Qi Shenwu) held the court in his grip.

sentences.zh: 太祖請往觀之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke asked to go and observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai asked leave to visit him and take his measure.

sentences.zh: 旣至幷州，齊神武問岳軍事，太祖口對雄辯，齊神武以為非常人，欲留之。

translations.literal: When he reached Bing Province, Gao Huan questioned him about Yue's military affairs; the Grand Duke answered with forceful eloquence, and Gao Huan judged him no ordinary man and wished to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: At Bingzhou, Gao Huan questioned him about Helba Yue's forces. Yuwen Tai replied with sharp eloquence; Gao Huan marked him as extraordinary and tried to keep him.

sentences.zh: 太祖詭陳忠款，乃得反命，遂星言就道。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke feigned earnest loyalty and thereby obtained permission to return with his mission; he then traveled day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai played the loyal subject convincingly, secured leave to depart, and raced homeward without pause.

sentences.zh: 齊神武果遣追之，至關，不及。

translations.literal: Gao Huan indeed sent men in pursuit, but they reached the pass too late.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan did send pursuers, but they reached the pass after Yuwen Tai was gone.

sentences.zh: 太祖還謂岳曰：「高歡非人臣也。

translations.literal: On returning, the Grand Duke said to Yue: "Gao Huan is no loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp Yuwen Tai told Yue: "Gao Huan is no man to serve a throne faithfully.

sentences.zh: 逆謀所以未發者，憚公兄弟耳。

translations.literal: The reason his treason has not yet broken out is that he fears you and your brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He has not yet moved against the dynasty only because he fears you and your brothers.

sentences.zh: 然凡欲立大功，匡社稷，未有不因地勢，總英雄，而能克成者也。

translations.literal: Yet whoever would achieve great deeds and restore the altars of state has never failed to rely on terrain, gather heroes, and thereby bring success to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Still, no one wins great victories or saves a dynasty without holding ground, rallying able men, and building from there.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅本實庸材，遭逢際會，遂叨任委，旣無憂國之心，亦不為高歡所忌。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue is by nature a mediocrity who, meeting with opportunity, came to hold high office; he has neither a heart that cares for the state nor does Gao Huan regard him as a threat.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue is a mediocrity elevated by chance; he cares nothing for the realm, and Gao Huan does not fear him.

sentences.zh: 但為之備，圖之不難。

translations.literal: If we guard against him and plot his downfall, it will not be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Keep watch and move against him, and the thing is not hard.

sentences.zh: 今費也頭控弦之騎不下一萬，夏州刺史斛拔彌俄突勝兵之士三千餘人，及靈州刺史曹泥，並恃其僻遠，常懷異望。

translations.literal: Now the Fei Yetou have no fewer than ten thousand mounted archers; Hubo Mi'etu, governor of Xia Province, has more than three thousand picked troops; and Cao Ni, governor of Ling Province—all rely on their remote positions and often harbor separate ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The Fei Yetou can field ten thousand bowmen; Xiazhou governor Hubo Mi'etu commands three thousand elite soldiers; and Lingzhou governor Cao Ni—all cling to distant posts and nurse private designs.

sentences.zh: 河西流民紇豆陵伊利等，戶口富實，未奉朝風。

translations.literal: The displaced people west of the river, Hedouling Yili and others, are rich in households and population and have not yet submitted to the court's influence.
translations.idiomatic: West of the river, refugees such as Hedouling Yili are numerous and wealthy and still stand outside imperial sway.

sentences.zh: 今若移軍近隴，扼其要害，示之以威，服之以德，卽可收其士馬，以實吾軍。

translations.literal: If we now shift the army close to Longyou, seize the key points, display our might, and win them with virtue, we can at once gather their warriors and horses to strengthen our forces.
translations.idiomatic: Move the army up to Longyou, hold the choke points, show force and offer favor, and we can absorb their fighters and horses into our own ranks.

sentences.zh: 西輯氐羌，北撫沙塞，還軍長安，匡輔魏室，此桓文舉也。

translations.literal: In the west gather the Di and Qiang; in the north pacify the desert frontier; then return the army to Chang'an and support the Wei house—this is an achievement like that of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the Di and Qiang in the west, calm the northern marches, march back to Chang'an, and uphold the Wei throne—the deed of a Huan or a Wen.

sentences.zh: 」岳大悅，復遣太祖詣闕請事，密陳其狀。

translations.literal: " Yue was greatly pleased and again sent the Grand Duke to the court to request instructions and secretly report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was elated and sent Yuwen Tai to court to seek approval and lay out the plan in secret.

sentences.zh: 魏帝深納之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor of Wei embraced the proposal wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 加太祖武衛將軍，還令報岳。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke was further made General of Martial Guards and sent back to report to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was promoted to general of martial guards and dispatched to relay the answer to Yue.

sentences.zh: 岳遂引軍西次平涼，謀於其衆曰：「夏州鄰接寇賊，須加綏撫，安得良刺史以鎮之？

translations.literal: Yue then led his army west and encamped at Pingliang, consulting his officers: "Xia Province borders on bandits and must be firmly pacified—where shall we find a good governor to hold it?
translations.idiomatic: Yue marched west to Pingliang and asked his officers: "Xiazhou lies against the frontier and needs steady rule—who is fit to govern it?

sentences.zh: 」衆皆曰：「宇文左丞卽其人也。

translations.literal: " All said: "Commissioner Yuwen on the left is the man.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered as one: "Left Director Yuwen is the man.

sentences.zh: 」岳曰：「左丞吾之左右手也，如何可廢。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "The left director is my right hand—how can I do without him?
translations.idiomatic: " Yue replied: "He is my right hand—I cannot spare him.

sentences.zh: 」沉吟累日，乃從衆議。

translations.literal: " He hesitated for many days, then yielded to the officers' opinion.
translations.idiomatic: " After days of hesitation he bowed to their choice.

sentences.zh: 於是表太祖為使持節、武衛將軍、夏州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized the throne to appoint the Grand Duke as bearer of the staff of authority, General of Martial Guards, and Governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Yuwen Tai as bearer of the staff of authority, general of martial guards, and governor of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖至州，伊利望風款附，而曹泥猶通使於齊神武。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke reached the province, Yili submitted at the first news of his arrival, while Cao Ni still maintained contact with Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Xiazhou, Yili surrendered at once; Cao Ni, however, still exchanged messages with Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 魏永熙三年春正月，岳欲討曹泥，遣都督趙貴至夏州與太祖計事。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year of Yongxi of Wei, Yue wished to attack Cao Ni and dispatched the commander Zhao Gui to Xia Province to consult with the Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, first month of Wei Yongxi 3 (534), Yue planned to attack Cao Ni and sent Commander Zhao Gui to Xiazhou to confer with Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「曹泥孤城阻遠，未足為憂。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said: "Cao Ni holds a lone city far away—not enough to worry over.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai said: "Cao Ni sits in a distant walled town—hardly worth concern.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅怙衆密邇，貪而無信，必將為患，願早圖之。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue relies on his numbers and lies close at hand; he is greedy and faithless and is sure to become a danger—I beg that we move against him early.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue is near, overconfident in his numbers, greedy and untrustworthy, and bound to turn dangerous. Strike him first.

sentences.zh: 」岳不聽，遂與悅俱討泥。

translations.literal: " Helba Yue would not listen and went with Houmochen Yue together to attack Ni.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue refused and marched with Houmochen Yue against Cao Ni instead.

sentences.zh: 二月，至於河曲，岳果為悅所害。

translations.literal: In the second month, when they reached the bend of the river, Helba Yue was indeed killed by Houmochen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, at the river bend, Helba Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 其士衆散還平涼，唯大都督趙貴率部曲收岳屍還營。

translations.literal: His soldiers scattered back toward Pingliang; only the chief commander Zhao Gui led his personal following to recover Yue's body and return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke up toward Pingliang; only Chief Commander Zhao Gui gathered his household troops, recovered Yue's body, and brought it back to camp.

sentences.zh: 於是三軍未有所屬，諸將以都督寇洛年最長，相與推洛以總兵事。

translations.literal: At that time the three armies had no leader; the generals, because the commander Kou Luo was the eldest in years, together pushed Luo to take overall command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With the host leaderless, the generals chose Kou Luo, the senior among them by age, to command.

sentences.zh: 洛素無雄略，威令不行，乃謂諸將曰：「洛智能本闕，不宜統御，近者迫於羣議，推相攝領，今請避位，更擇賢材。

translations.literal: Luo by nature lacked heroic strategy, and his authority did not hold; he therefore said to the generals: "My talent and intelligence are inherently deficient—I am unfit to command. Recently, pressed by the officers' consensus, I accepted the interim post; now I ask to step aside and choose a worthier man.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo lacked bold command and could not enforce his orders. He told the officers: "I am not the man for this. You pushed me into acting commander; let me yield the post to someone better.

sentences.zh: 」於是趙貴言於衆曰：「元帥忠公盡節，暴於朝野，勳業未就，奄罹凶酷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zhao Gui spoke to the assembly: "The marshal loyally gave his life for the state, his martyrdom plain to court and camp alike; his great work unfinished, he was suddenly cut down.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Gui then addressed the host: "Our marshal died loyal to the throne before all eyes, his great task unfinished, struck down without warning.

sentences.zh: 豈唯國喪良宰，固亦衆無所依。

translations.literal: It is not only the realm that has lost a fine minister—the host too has no one to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: The court has lost a great minister, and we soldiers have lost our anchor.

sentences.zh: 必欲糾合同盟，復讐雪恥，須擇賢者，總統諸軍。

translations.literal: If we truly mean to rally the alliance, avenge the wrong, and wipe away the disgrace, we must choose a worthy man to command all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: To reunite the alliance, take revenge, and restore honor, we need a leader worthy of the whole host.

sentences.zh: 舉非其人，則大事難集，雖欲立忠建義，其可得乎。

translations.literal: If the choice is not the right man, great affairs will be hard to accomplish; even if we wish to establish loyalty and righteousness, how can it be done?
translations.idiomatic: Choose wrongly and the cause collapses; loyalty alone will not save us.

sentences.zh: 竊觀宇文夏州，英姿不世，雄謨冠時，遠邇歸心，士卒用命。

translations.literal: I have observed Commissioner Yuwen of Xia Province—his heroic bearing unmatched in the age, his bold designs foremost in the time; near and far turn to him, and the soldiers obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yuwen Tai of Xiazhou: a peerless hero, the boldest strategist of the day, trusted by men near and far, obeyed without question by his troops.

sentences.zh: 加以法令齊肅，賞罰嚴明，真足恃也。

translations.literal: Moreover his laws and orders are uniform and strict, his rewards and punishments clear and severe—he is truly one on whom we can rely.
translations.idiomatic: His discipline is firm, his rewards and punishments exact—he is a man we can lean on.

sentences.zh: 今若告喪，必來赴難，因而奉之，則大事集矣。

translations.literal: If we now announce the mourning, he is sure to come to our aid; if we then install him as leader, the great affair will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Send word of the death and he will come; put him at the head of the host and the cause is won.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆稱善。

translations.literal: " All the generals praised the plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals approved unanimously.

sentences.zh: 乃命赫連達馳至夏州，告太祖曰：「侯莫陳悅不顧盟誓，棄恩背德，賊害忠良，羣情憤惋，控告無所。

translations.literal: They then ordered Helian Da to ride at speed to Xia Province and tell the Grand Duke: "Houmochen Yue has spurned the oath of alliance, cast off kindness and betrayed trust, and murdered a loyal minister; the host is furious and aggrieved, with nowhere to lodge its grievance.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Helian Da posthaste to Xiazhou with this message for Yuwen Tai: "Houmochen Yue broke his oath, betrayed his benefactor, and killed a loyal minister. The army burns with outrage and has no one to answer to.

sentences.zh: 公昔居管轄，恩信著聞，今無小無大，咸願推奉。

translations.literal: You once held authority here, renowned for kindness and good faith; now great and small alike wish to install you as leader.
translations.idiomatic: You governed here before and are known for mercy and trust; every man, high or low, wants you as commander.

sentences.zh: 衆之思公，引日成歲，願勿稽留，以慰衆望也。

translations.literal: The host's longing for you has stretched from days into months; we beg you not to delay and thereby comfort the host's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: We have waited for you day after day, month after month—do not linger and disappoint the host.

sentences.zh: 」太祖將赴之，夏州吏民咸泣請曰：「聞悅今在

translations.literal: " The Grand Duke was about to go when the officials and people of Xia Province all wept and pleaded: "We hear that Yue is now at
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai prepared to depart, but Xiazhou's officials and people wept and begged him: "We hear Houmochen Yue is now at

translations.literal: (Yong)
translations.idiomatic: (Yong)

sentences.zh: 〔水〕洛，去平涼不遠。

translations.literal: [Shui]luo, not far from Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuoluo, not far from Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 若已有賀拔公之衆，則圖之實難。

translations.literal: If he already has Helba Yue's troops, then to plot against him will truly be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If he has already taken Helba Yue's army, moving against him will be far harder.

sentences.zh: 願且停留，以觀其變。

translations.literal: We beg you to stay awhile and observe how matters change.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to remain here awhile and watch how events unfold.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「悅旣害元帥，自應乘勢直據平涼，而反趑趄，屯兵水洛，吾知其無能為也。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Tai said: "Yue has already killed the marshal; he ought to seize the moment and march straight on Pingliang, yet instead he hesitates and camps at Shuoluo—I know he can accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai replied: "Houmochen Yue murdered the marshal, yet instead of pressing straight for Pingliang he dithers at Shuoluo. He is finished.

sentences.zh: 且難得易失者時也，不俟終日者幾也，今不早赴，將恐衆心自離。

translations.literal: What is hard to gain and easy to lose is time; what does not wait even a full day is opportunity. If we do not go early, I fear the host's hearts will scatter of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Time once lost is gone; opportunity will not wait until evening. Delay now and the army will melt away.

sentences.zh: 」都督彌姐元進規欲應悅，密圖太祖。

translations.literal: " The commander Mizhi Yuanjin planned to join Yue and secretly plotted against Yuwen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: " Commander Mizhi Yuanjin meant to side with Yue and secretly moved against Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 事發，斬之。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃率帳下輕騎，馳赴平涼。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai then led the light cavalry of his personal guard and raced to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai gathered his household light cavalry and galloped for Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 時齊神武遣長史侯景招引岳衆，太祖至安定，遇之，謂景曰：「賀拔公雖死，宇文泰尚存，卿何為也？

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu, had sent his chief clerk Hou Jing to win over Helba Yue's troops. When Yuwen Tai reached Anding he met Jing and said to him: "Though Helba Gong is dead, Yuwen Tai yet lives—what are you about?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had sent his chief clerk Hou Jing to recruit Helba Yue's army. At Anding, Yuwen Tai confronted him: "Helba Yue is dead, but I am still here—what do you think you are doing?

sentences.zh: 」景失色，對曰：「我猶箭耳，隨人所射，安能自裁。

translations.literal: " Jing turned pale and answered: "I am but an arrow—whichever way men shoot, that way I fly. How could I decide for myself?
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Jing blanched and said: "I am only an arrow in another man's bow—I go where I am sent. I cannot choose for myself.

sentences.zh: 」景於此卽還。

translations.literal: " At that Jing turned back at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Jing withdrew on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太祖至平涼，哭岳甚慟。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Tai reached Pingliang, he wept for Yue with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang Yuwen Tai mourned Yue with wrenching grief.

sentences.zh: 將士且悲且喜曰：「宇文公至，無所憂矣。」

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, both sorrowful and glad, said: "Lord Yuwen has come—we need fear nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men wept and cheered together: "Yuwen Tai is here—our troubles are over."

sentences.zh: 於時，魏孝武帝將圖齊神武，聞岳被害，遣武衛將軍元毗宣旨慰勞，追岳軍還洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, planning to move against Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu, heard that Yue had been killed and dispatched the Martial Guard General Yuan Pi to proclaim the imperial will, offer comfort, and recall Yue's army to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, preparing to strike at Gao Huan, learned of Yue's murder and sent Martial Guard General Yuan Pi to comfort the host and order Yue's army back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 毗到平涼，會諸將已推太祖。

translations.literal: When Pi reached Pingliang, he found the generals had already chosen Yuwen Tai as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Pi arrived at Pingliang to find the generals had already elevated Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅亦被勅追還，悅旣附齊神武，不肯應召。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue too had been ordered to return, but Yue, having already attached himself to Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu, refused the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue had also been recalled, but having thrown in with Gao Huan he refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂諸將曰：「侯莫陳悅枉害忠良，復不應詔命，此國之大賊，豈可容之！

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai said to the generals: "Houmochen Yue wrongfully killed a loyal minister and again refuses the imperial command—this is the realm's great villain. How can he be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai told his officers: "Houmochen Yue murdered a loyal minister and now defies the throne—a traitor to the realm. He cannot be allowed to live.

sentences.zh: 」乃命諸軍戒嚴，將以討悅。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the armies to stand on alert and prepared to punish Yue.
translations.idiomatic: " He put the host under arms and prepared to march against Yue.

sentences.zh: 及元毗還，太祖表於魏帝曰：「臣前以故關西大都督臣岳，竭誠奉國，橫罹非命，三軍喪氣，朝野痛惜。

translations.literal: When Yuan Pi returned, Yuwen Tai memorialized the emperor of Wei: "Your subject's former superior, the late Grand Commissioner of the Western Passes, my lord Yue, served the state with utter loyalty yet met a violent end; the three armies lost heart, and court and countryside alike mourned.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Pi departed, Yuwen Tai wrote the emperor: "Your late commissioner Helba Yue served the throne with perfect loyalty and was cut down without cause. The army lost heart; the court and the people grieved.

sentences.zh: 都督寇洛等，銜冤茹戚，志雪讐恥。

translations.literal: Commander Kou Luo and the others nursed their grievance and bitterness, resolved to wipe away the shame and avenge the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo and the other commanders burned with outrage and swore to avenge the wrong.

sentences.zh: 以臣昔同幕府，苦賜要結。

translations.literal: Because I once served in the same headquarters, they pressed upon me a binding pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing I had served in the same headquarters, they bound me to their cause.

sentences.zh: 臣便以今月十四日，輕來赴軍，當發之時，已有別表，旣為衆情所逼，權掌兵事。

translations.literal: I therefore came lightly to the army on the fourteenth of this month; when I set out I had already submitted a separate memorial, yet once pressed by the host's will I took command of the troops in interim authority.
translations.idiomatic: I came to the host on the fourteenth of this month—having already filed a separate report—and, pressed by the army's will, assumed interim command.

sentences.zh: 詔召岳軍入京，此乃為國良策。

translations.literal: The edict summoning Yue's army to the capital is indeed sound policy for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Your order to bring Yue's army east is wise statecraft.

sentences.zh: 但高歡之衆，已至河東，侯莫陳悅猶在水洛。

translations.literal: Yet Gao Huan's forces have already reached Hedong, and Houmochen Yue still holds Shuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: But Gao Huan's troops are already at Hedong, and Houmochen Yue still camps at Shuoluo.

sentences.zh: 況此軍士多是關西之人，皆戀鄉邑，不願東下。

translations.literal: Moreover most of these soldiers are men of Guanxi who cling to their home districts and do not wish to march east.
translations.idiomatic: Most of these men are westerners who yearn for home and dread marching east.

sentences.zh: 今逼以上命。

translations.literal: Now they are forced by a command from above.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are driven by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 悉令赴關，悅躡其後，歡邀其前，首尾受敵，其勢危矣。

translations.literal: If all are ordered to the passes, Yue will press from the rear and Huan will block the front—they will be struck at both ends and the peril will be extreme.
translations.idiomatic: March them to the passes and Yue will harry their rear while Huan blocks their front—caught between two enemies, they will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 臣殞身王事，誠所甘心，恐敗國殄人，所損更大。

translations.literal: Your subject would gladly give his life in royal service, yet I fear that ruining the state and wasting the people would be the greater loss.
translations.idiomatic: I would gladly die in your service, but I fear the greater harm would be to ruin the army and waste the realm.

sentences.zh: 乞少停緩，更思後圖，徐事誘導，漸就東引。

translations.literal: I beg a brief delay to reconsider later plans, to guide the men gradually and draw them east by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: I beg a little time to reconsider, to coax the men eastward step by step.

sentences.zh: 」太祖志在討悅，而未測朝旨，且兵衆未集，假此為詞。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Tai's aim was to punish Yue, yet he had not gauged the court's intent and his troops were not yet gathered; he used this as his plea.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai meant to strike Yue, but the court's mind was uncertain and his forces not yet assembled—so he pleaded for time.

sentences.zh: 因與元毗及諸將刑牲盟誓，同獎王室。

translations.literal: He then joined Yuan Pi and the generals in sacrificing an animal and swearing an oath to support the royal house together.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Yuan Pi and the generals in a blood oath to uphold the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，賀拔岳營於河曲，有軍吏獨行，忽見一老翁，鬚眉皓素，謂之曰：「賀拔岳雖復據有此衆，然終無所成。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Helba Yue had encamped at Hequ, a staff officer walking alone suddenly saw an old man with white beard and brows who said to him: "Though Helba Yue again holds this host, in the end he will achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Helba Yue camped at Hequ, a staff officer walking alone met an old man with snow-white beard and brows who said: "Helba Yue may command this army, yet he will never succeed.

sentences.zh: 當有一宇文家從東北來，後必大盛。

translations.literal: There will be a man of the Yuwen clan coming from the northeast; afterward he will flourish greatly.
translations.idiomatic: A Yuwen will come from the northeast and rise to greatness.

sentences.zh: 」言訖不見。

translations.literal: " When he had spoken, he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he disappeared.

sentences.zh: 此吏恒與所親言之，至是方驗。

translations.literal: The officer had often told those close to him of this; only now was it verified.
translations.idiomatic: The officer had told his friends again and again; only now did they see it fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 魏帝詔太祖曰：「賀拔岳旣殞，士衆未有所歸，卿可為大都督，卽相統領。

translations.literal: The emperor of Wei addressed Yuwen Tai: "Now that Helba Yue has fallen, the soldiers have no leader—you may serve as grand commander and take charge at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote Yuwen Tai: "Helba Yue is gone and the host is leaderless. Take command as grand commander at once.

sentences.zh: 知欲漸就東下，良不可言。

translations.literal: I know you mean to move gradually east—well said.
translations.idiomatic: Your plan to move east by degrees is exactly right.

sentences.zh: 今亦征侯莫陳悅士馬入京。

translations.literal: Now summon Houmochen Yue's troops and horses to the capital as well.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Houmochen Yue's forces to the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 若其不來，朕當親自致罰。

translations.literal: If he does not come, I myself will inflict punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If he refuses, I will punish him in person.

sentences.zh: 宜體此意，不過淹留。

translations.literal: Take this to heart and do not linger overlong.
translations.idiomatic: Heed this—and do not delay overlong.

sentences.zh: 」太祖又表曰：「侯莫陳悅違天逆理，酷害良臣，自以專戮罪重，不恭詔命，阻兵水洛，強梁秦隴。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Tai memorialized again: "Houmochen Yue defies Heaven and violates reason, cruelly killing a good minister. Knowing his crime of unauthorized execution is grave, he disobeys the imperial command, blocks the army at Shuoluo, and acts the tyrant in Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai wrote again: "Houmochen Yue defies Heaven and butchered a loyal minister. Knowing his crime of summary execution is capital, he rejects your summons, holds Shuoluo with armed force, and terrorizes Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 臣以大宥旣班，忍抑私憾，頻問悅及都督可朱渾元等歸闕早晚，而悅並維縶使人，不聽反報。

translations.literal: Your subject, though the great pardon has been proclaimed, suppressed private hatred and repeatedly asked Yue and Commander Kezhuhun Yuan when they would return to court—yet Yue bound and detained my envoys and would not allow them to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court has proclaimed a general amnesty, I swallowed private grief and repeatedly asked Yue and Kezhuhun Yuan when they would come to court—yet Yue seized my messengers and sent no answer.

sentences.zh: 觀其指趣，勢必異圖。

translations.literal: Judging by his intent, he is certain to harbor a different design.
translations.idiomatic: By his conduct he plainly intends treason.

sentences.zh: 臣正為此，未敢自拔。

translations.literal: It is for this reason that I have not dared withdraw on my own.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have not dared march east alone.

sentences.zh: 兼順衆情，乞少停緩。

translations.literal: Following the host's sentiment as well, I beg a brief delay.
translations.idiomatic: The army demands the same—and I beg a little more time.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃與悅書責之曰：

translations.literal: " Yuwen Tai then wrote Yue a letter rebuking him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai then sent Yue a letter of rebuke:

sentences.zh: 頃者正光之末，天下沸騰，塵飛河朔，霧塞荊沔。

translations.literal: In recent times, at the end of the Zhengguang era, the realm boiled over; dust flew over Heshuo and mist choked Jing and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Zhengguang the empire erupted in chaos—war swept the Yellow River northlands and turmoil choked the middle Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 故將軍賀拔公攘袂勃起，志寧宇縣。

translations.literal: The late General Helba Gong rolled up his sleeves and rose, his will set on pacifying the realm.
translations.idiomatic: General Helba Yue rose in arms, resolved to restore order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 授戈南指，拯皇靈於已墜；

translations.literal: He took spear in hand and pointed south, saving the imperial spirit as it was falling;
translations.idiomatic: Spear in hand he marched south and snatched the throne back from ruin;

sentences.zh: 擁旄西邁，濟百姓於淪胥。

translations.literal: bearing his banner he marched west, delivering the people from drowning.
translations.idiomatic: banner raised he marched west and pulled the people back from destruction.

sentences.zh: 西顧無憂，繄公是賴。

translations.literal: The west looked on without fear—on him alone it relied.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier rested secure—entirely on his strength.

sentences.zh: 勳茂賞隆，遂征關右。

translations.literal: His merit was abundant and his rewards lofty; he thereupon campaigned into Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Honored for towering merit, he then secured the western passes.

sentences.zh: 此乃行路所知，不籍一二談也。

translations.literal: This is what travelers know—it needs no lengthy argument.
translations.idiomatic: Every traveler knows this—it needs no long proof.

sentences.zh: 君實名微行薄，本無遠量。

translations.literal: You, sir, were in name slight and in conduct thin, with no far-reaching capacity by nature.
translations.idiomatic: You were obscure and insignificant, a man of no vision.

sentences.zh: 故將軍降遷高之志，篤匯征之理，乃申啟朝廷，薦君為隴右行臺。

translations.literal: The late general lowered his lofty intent and earnestly gathered the principles of enlistment; he then reported to the court and recommended you as commissioner of the Longyou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The general set aside his own ambition and pressed your case before the throne, recommending you as commissioner for Longyou.

sentences.zh: 朝議以君功名闕然，未之許也。

translations.literal: The court considered your achievements empty and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The court saw you had done nothing and refused.

sentences.zh: 遂頻煩請謁，至於再三。

translations.literal: He then repeatedly petitioned, again and again.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded again and again until the court yielded.

sentences.zh: 天子難違上將，便相聽許。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, hard pressed by his chief general, at last consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unable to refuse his champion, at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 是亦遐邇共知，不復煩之翰墨。

translations.literal: Near and far alike know this—it need not be rehearsed in writing.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm knows this—there is no need to rehearse it on paper.

sentences.zh: 縱使木石為心，猶當知感；

translations.literal: Even were one's heart stone or wood, one ought still to know gratitude;
translations.idiomatic: Stone and timber would feel gratitude;

sentences.zh: 況在生靈，安能無愧。

translations.literal: how much more among living men—how could one be without shame?
translations.idiomatic: how then can any living man face the world without shame?

sentences.zh: 加以王室多故，高氏專權，主上虛心，寄隆晉鄭。

translations.literal: Moreover the royal house has many troubles and the Gao clan monopolizes power; the sovereign holds an open mind and has entrusted you as once Jin and Zheng were entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is beset by crisis and the Gao faction grips power; the emperor has placed his trust in you as once in the ministers of Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 君復與故將軍同受密旨，屢結盟約，期於畢力，共匡時難。

translations.literal: You again received secret orders together with the late general, repeatedly swore alliance, and pledged to exert your full strength and together right the age's peril.
translations.idiomatic: You took secret orders with the general, swore alliance upon alliance, and pledged to give your all to save the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 而貌恭心狠，妒勝嫉賢，口血未乾，匕首已發。

translations.literal: Yet in appearance respectful, in heart cruel—you envied the victorious and hated the worthy; the oath-blood was not yet dry before the dagger was already drawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you bowed in false courtesy while plotting murder—jealous of merit, hating the able; the blood of your oath had barely dried before you struck.

sentences.zh: 協黨國賊，共危本朝，孤恩負誓，有靦面目。

translations.literal: You joined the traitor to the state in endangering the court, betrayed kindness and broke your oath—have you any face left?
translations.idiomatic: You conspired with the realm's enemy, betrayed your benefactor, and broke your oath—have you no shame?

sentences.zh: 豈不上畏於天，下慚於地！

translations.literal: Do you not fear Heaven above and blush before Earth below!
translations.idiomatic: Do you not fear Heaven above and blush before Earth below!

sentences.zh: 吾以弱才，猥當藩牧，蒙朝廷拔擢之恩，荷故將軍國士之遇。

translations.literal: I, with my weak talent, have unworthily held a frontier post, receiving the court's grace in raising me and the late general's treatment of me as a national champion.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of little talent, unworthily holding a frontier post—raised by the court and honored by the general as a champion of the realm.

sentences.zh: 聞問之日，魂守驚馳。

translations.literal: On the day I heard the news, my soul trembled in alarm as I raced to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard the news my soul shook and I raced to answer.

sentences.zh: 便陳啟天朝，暫來奔赴，衆情所推，遂當戎重。

translations.literal: At once I reported to the heavenly court and came temporarily to join the army; pressed by the host's will, I thereupon took the weight of command.
translations.idiomatic: I reported to the throne and came at once; the army pressed me, and I took command.

sentences.zh: 比有敕旨，召吾還闕，亦有別詔，令君入朝。

translations.literal: Recently there have been imperial orders summoning me back to court, and separate edicts ordering you to enter the capital as well.
translations.idiomatic: The throne has summoned me back to court and issued separate orders for you to come as well.

sentences.zh: 雖操行無聞，而年齒已宿。

translations.literal: Though your conduct is unknown to fame, your years are already advanced.
translations.idiomatic: You may lack renown, but you are no longer young.

sentences.zh: 今日進退，唯君是視。

translations.literal: Whether we advance or retreat today depends on you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Whether we march east or stand fast now rests with you alone.

sentences.zh: 君若督率所部，自山隴東邁，吾亦總勒師徒，北道還闕。

translations.literal: If you lead your troops east from the mountains and Long, I too will gather the host and return north to court.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your men east from the Long Mountains and I will march north to the capital with the host.

sentences.zh: 共追廉、藺之跡，同慕寇、賈之風。

translations.literal: Together we shall follow the tracks of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru and alike admire the spirit of Kou Yun and Jia Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Let us follow the example of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru and honor the loyalty of Kou Yun and Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 如其首鼠兩端，不時奉詔，專戮違旨，國有常刑，枕戈坐甲，指日相見。

translations.literal: If instead you waver like a rat at both ends and do not obey the command in timely fashion, unauthorized execution in defiance of the edict carries the state's fixed penalty—I sit with spear in hand and shall meet you within days.
translations.idiomatic: But if you hedge and delay, summary execution in defiance of the throne is a capital crime—I sit armed and will meet you within days.

sentences.zh: 幸圖利害，無貽噬臍。

translations.literal: Consider profit and harm carefully—do not bring upon yourself the fate of being devoured from within.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh your interest carefully—do not invite the doom of a beast devoured by its own kind.

sentences.zh: 悅旣懼太祖謀己，詐為詔書與秦州刺史万俟普撥，令與悅為黨援。

translations.literal: Yue, fearing Yuwen Tai's designs against him, forged an imperial edict to Mozhan Pobo, governor of Qin Province, ordering him to join Yue as an ally.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yuwen Tai, Yue forged an imperial edict to Qinzhou governor Mozhan Pobo, urging him to join as ally.

sentences.zh: 普撥疑之，封詔以呈太祖。

translations.literal: Pobo doubted it, sealed the edict, and presented it to Yuwen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhan Pobo suspected fraud, sealed the document, and sent it to Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖表之曰：「臣自奉詔總平涼之師，責重憂深，不遑啟處。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai memorialized: "Since receiving the edict to command the Pingliang army, my burden of responsibility and depth of worry have left me no leisure for rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai reported to the throne: "Since I took command at Pingliang, the weight of duty has allowed me no rest.

sentences.zh: 訓兵秣馬，唯思竭力。

translations.literal: In drilling troops and feeding horses, I think only of exerting my full strength.
translations.idiomatic: I drill the men and ready the horses and think only of giving my all.

sentences.zh: 前以人戀本土，侯莫陳悅窺窬進退，量度且宜住此。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the men yearn for their home districts and Houmochen Yue watches for any shift in our movements, I judged it best for the moment to remain here.
translations.idiomatic: Because the men cling to their homes and Houmochen Yue watches every move, I judged it best to hold here for now.

sentences.zh: 今若召悅授以內官，臣列旆東轅，匪朝伊夕。

translations.literal: Now if Yue is summoned and given an inner-court post, I shall turn my banners east—not tomorrow but today.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Yue to a court appointment and I will turn east at once—not tomorrow, but today.

sentences.zh: 朝廷若以悅堪為邊扞，乞處以瓜、涼一藩。

translations.literal: If the court considers Yue fit to guard the frontier, I beg that he be given one of the Guazhou or Liangzhou commands.
translations.idiomatic: If the court believes Yue can guard the frontier, give him Guazhou or Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 不然，則終致猜虞，於事無益。」

translations.literal: Otherwise suspicion will end in distrust, and nothing will be gained.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise suspicion will poison everything and nothing will be gained."

sentences.zh: 初，原州刺史史歸為岳所親任，河曲之變，反為悅守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi Gui, governor of Yuan Province, had been trusted and employed by Yue; at the crisis at the river bend he turned instead to hold the city for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhou governor Shi Gui had been Yue's trusted man; at the river-bend crisis he defected and held the city for Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅遣其黨王伯和、成次安將兵二千人助歸鎮原州。

translations.literal: Yue sent his partisans Wang Bohe and Cheng Ci'an with two thousand troops to help Gui garrison Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Wang Bohe and Cheng Ci'an with two thousand men to reinforce Shi Gui at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣都督侯莫陳崇率輕騎一千襲歸，擒之，幷獲次安、伯和等，送於平涼。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai dispatched Commander Houmochen Chong with one thousand light cavalry to strike Gui, captured him, and also took Ci'an, Bohe, and the others, sending them to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent Houmochen Chong with a thousand light cavalry, seized Shi Gui, and captured Ci'an, Wang Bohe, and the rest, sending them to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 太祖表崇行原州事。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai memorialized that Chong should administer Yuan Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai recommended Houmochen Chong to govern Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 万俟普撥又遣其將叱乾保洛領二千騎來從軍。

translations.literal: Mozhan Pobo also sent his commander Chi'gan Baoluo with two thousand cavalry to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhan Pobo sent his commander Chi'gan Baoluo with two thousand horsemen to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 三月，太祖進軍至原州。

translations.literal: In the third month Yuwen Tai advanced the army to Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yuwen Tai marched on Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 衆軍悉集，諭以討悅之意，士卒莫不懷憤。

translations.literal: When the host had fully gathered, he declared the intent to punish Yue, and the soldiers all nursed indignation.
translations.idiomatic: With the host assembled, he announced the campaign against Yue, and every soldier burned with outrage.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃表曰：「臣聞誓死酬恩，覆宗報主，人倫所急，赴蹈如歸。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai then memorialized: "Your subject has heard that to swear death in repaying kindness and to overturn one's clan in answering one's lord is what human relations most urgently require—men rush to it as to returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai wrote the throne: "To repay kindness with one's life and answer one's lord even at the cost of one's house is the first duty of a man—men run to it as homeward.

sentences.zh: 自大都督臣岳歿後，臣頻奉詔還闕，秣馬戒途，志不俟旦。

translations.literal: Since the death of the Grand Commissioner my lord Yue, I have repeatedly received orders to return to court; I have fed the horses and prepared the road, my will not waiting even for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Since Helba Yue's death I have again and again been ordered back to court; I have fed the horses and readied the march, eager to depart before dawn.

sentences.zh: 直以督將已下，咸稱賀拔公視我如子，今讐恥未報，亦何面目以處世間，若得一雪冤酷，萬死無恨。

translations.literal: Only because the commanders and officers below all said Helba Gong treated me as a son—now that shame and vengeance are unavenged, with what face could I remain in the world? If I may once wipe away this cruel wrong, I would die ten thousand deaths without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Only because every officer said Helba Yue treated me as a son—with vengeance unpaid, how could I show my face in the world? Give me one chance to avenge him and I would die without regret.

sentences.zh: 且悅外附強臣，內違朝旨。

translations.literal: Moreover Yue outwardly attaches himself to a powerful minister while inwardly defying the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yue serves a powerful minister abroad while defying the throne at home.

sentences.zh: 臣今上思逐惡之志，下遂節士之心，冀仗天威，為國除害。

translations.literal: Your subject now above cherishes the will to drive out evil and below fulfills the heart of a man of integrity, hoping to rely on Heaven's majesty to remove the harm to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now I honor the duty to destroy evil and fulfill the heart of a loyal man, trusting in Heaven's power to purge this threat to the realm.

sentences.zh: 小違大順，實在茲辰。

translations.literal: A small breach of the great order—the moment is truly now.
translations.idiomatic: A lesser duty must yield to the greater—the hour is now.

sentences.zh: 克定之後，伏待斧鉞。」

translations.literal: After victory is secured, I shall await the axe and halberd in submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign is won, I will submit myself to judgment."

sentences.zh: 夏四月，引兵上隴，留兄子導為都督，鎮原州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer he led the army up the Long, leaving his elder brother's son Dao as commander to garrison Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he marched up the Long, leaving his nephew Dao to hold Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍令嚴肅，秋毫無犯，百姓大悅。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai's military orders were strict and severe; not a hair's breadth was violated, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai's discipline was iron; not a leaf was touched, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 識者知其有成。

translations.literal: Those who understood the signs knew he would succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Men who read the signs knew victory was at hand.

sentences.zh: 軍出木峽關，大雨雪，平地二尺。

translations.literal: When the army issued from Mukou Pass, heavy rain and snow fell; on level ground the depth was two feet.
translations.idiomatic: As the army crossed Mukou Pass, snow and rain fell until the flats lay two feet deep.

sentences.zh: 太祖知悅怯而多猜，乃倍道兼行，出其不意。
悅果疑其左右有異志者，左右亦不安，衆遂離貳。
聞大軍且至，退保略陽，留一萬餘人據守水洛。
太祖至水洛，命圍之，城降。
太祖卽率輕騎數百趣略陽，以臨悅軍，悅大懼，乃召其部將議之。
皆曰「此鋒不可當」，勸悅退保上邽以避之。
時南秦州刺史李弼亦在悅軍，乃間道遣使，請為內應。
其夜，悅出軍，軍中自驚潰，將卒或相率來降。
太祖縱兵奮擊，大破之。
虜獲萬餘人，馬八千疋。
悅與其子弟及麾下數十騎遁走。
太祖曰：「悅本與曹泥應接，不過走向靈州。
」乃令原州都督導邀其前，都督賀拔潁等追其後。
導至牽屯山追及悅，斬之。
太祖入上邽，收悅府庫，財物山積，皆以賞士卒，毫釐無所取。
左右竊一銀鏤甕以歸，太祖知而罪之，卽
〔剖〕賜將士，衆大悅。
時涼州刺史李叔仁為其民所執，舉州騷擾。
宕昌羌梁
〔仚〕定引吐谷渾寇金城。
渭州及南秦州氐、羌連結，所在蜂起。
南岐至于瓜、鄯，跨州據郡者，不可勝數。
太祖乃令李弼鎮原州，夏州刺史拔也惡蠔鎮南秦州，渭州刺史可朱渾元還鎮渭州，衛將軍趙貴行秦州事。
征豳、涇、東秦、岐四州粟以給軍。
齊神武聞秦隴克捷，乃遣使於太祖，甘言厚禮，深相倚結。
太祖拒而不納。
時齊神武已有異志，故魏帝深仗太祖。
乃徵二千騎鎮東雍州，助為聲援，仍令太祖稍引軍而東。
太祖乃遣大都督梁禦率步騎五千鎮河、渭合口，為圖河東之計。
太祖之討悅也，悅遣使請援於齊神武，神武使其都督韓軌將兵一萬據蒲阪，而雍州刺史賈顯送船與軌，請軌兵入關。
太祖因梁禦之東，乃逼召顯赴軍。
禦遂入雍州。
魏帝遣著作郎姚幼瑜持節勞軍，進太祖侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、關西大都督、略陽縣公，承制封拜，使持節如故。
於是以寇洛為涇州刺史，李弼為秦州刺史，前略陽郡守張獻為南岐州刺史。
盧待伯拒代，遣輕騎襲擒之，待伯自殺。
時魏帝方圖齊神武，又遣徵兵。
太祖乃令前秦州刺史駱超為大都督，率輕騎一千赴洛。
進授太祖兼尚書僕射、關西大行臺，餘官封如故。
太祖乃傳檄方鎮曰：
蓋聞陰陽遞用，盛衰相襲，苟當百六，無間三五。
皇家創曆，陶鑄蒼生，保安四海，仁育萬物。
運距孝昌，屯沴屢起，隴、冀騷動，燕、河狼顧。
雖靈命重啟，蕩定有期，而乘釁之徒，因生羽翼。
賊臣高歡，器識庸下，出自輿皂，罕聞禮義，直以一介鷹犬，效力戎行，靦冒恩私，遂階榮寵。
不能竭誠盡節，專挾姦回，乃勸爾朱榮行茲篡逆。
及榮以專政伏誅，世隆以凶黨外叛，歡苦相敦勉，令取京師。
又勸吐萬兒復為弒虐，暫立建明，以令天下，假推普泰，欲竊威權。
並歸廢斥，俱見酷害。
於是稱兵河北，假討爾朱，亟通表奏，云取讒賊。
旣行廢黜，遂將篡弒。
以人望未改，恐鼎鑊交及，乃求宗室，權允人心。
天方與魏，必將有主，翊戴聖明，誠非歡力。
而歡阻兵安忍，自以為功。
廣布腹心，跨州連郡，端揆禁闥，莫非親黨。
皆行貪虐，窫窳生人。
而舊將名臣，正人直士，橫生瘡痏，動掛網羅。
故武衛將軍伊琳，清貞剛毅，禁旅攸屬；
直閣將軍鮮于康仁，忠亮驍傑，爪牙斯在：歡收而戮之，曾无聞奏。
司空高乾，是其黨與，每相影響，謀危社稷。
但以姦志未從，恐先洩漏，乃密白朝廷，使殺高乾，方哭對其弟，稱天子橫戮。
孫騰、任祥，歡之心膂，並使入居樞近，伺國間隙，知歡逆謀將發，相繼逃歸，歡益加撫待，亦無陳白。
然歡入洛之始，本有姦謀。
令親人蔡儁作牧河、濟，厚相恩贍，以為東道主人。
故關西大都督、清水公賀拔岳，勳德隆重，興亡攸寄，歡好亂樂禍，深相忌毒，乃與侯莫陳悅陰圖陷害。
幕府以受律專征，便卽討戮。
歡知逆狀已露，稍懷旅距，遂遣蔡儁拒代，令竇泰佐之。
又遣侯景等云向白馬，輔世珍等徑趣石濟，高隆之、疋婁昭等屯據壺關，韓軌之徒擁衆蒲阪。
於是上書天子，數論得失，訾毀乘輿，威侮朝廷。
藉此微庸，冀茲大寶。
溪壑可盈，禍心不測。
或言徑赴荊楚，開疆於外；
或言分詣伊洛，取彼讒人；
或言欲來入關，與幕府決戰。
今聖明御運，天下清夷，百寮師師，四隩來暨。
人盡忠良，誰為君側？
而歡威福自己，生是亂階，緝構南箕，指鹿為馬，包藏凶逆，伺我神器。
是而可忍，孰不可容！
幕府折沖宇宙，親當受脤，銳師百萬，彀騎千羣，裹糧坐甲，唯敵是俟，義之所在，糜軀匪恡。
況頻有詔書，班告天下，稱歡逆亂，徵兵致伐。
今便分命將帥，應機進討。
或趣其要害，或襲其窟宅，電繞蛇擊，霧合星羅。
而歡違負天地，毒被人鬼，乘此掃蕩，易同俯拾。
歡若渡河，稍逼宗廟，則分命諸將，直取幷州，幕府躬自東轅，電赴伊洛；
若固其巢穴，未敢發動，亦命羣帥，百道俱前，轘裂賊臣，以謝天下。
其州鎮郡縣，率土人黎，或州鄉冠冕，或勳庸世濟，並宜捨逆歸順，立效軍門。
封賞之科，已有別格。
凡百君子，可不勉歟。
太祖謂諸將曰：「高歡雖智不足而詐有餘，今聲言欲西，其意在入洛。
吾欲令寇洛率馬步萬餘，自涇州東引；
王羆率甲士一萬，先據華州。
歡若西來，王羆足得抗拒；
如其入洛，寇洛卽襲汾晉。
吾便速駕，直赴京邑。
使其進有內顧之憂，退有被躡之勢。
一舉大定，此為上策。
」衆咸稱善。
秋七月，太祖帥衆發自高平，前軍至於弘農。
而齊神武稍逼京邑，魏帝親總六軍，屯於河橋，令左衛元斌之、領軍斛斯椿鎮武牢，遣使告太祖。
太祖謂左右曰：「高歡數日行八九百里，曉兵者所忌，正須乘便擊之。
而主上以萬乘之重，不能決戰，方緣津據守。
且長河萬里，扞禦為難，若一處得度，大事去矣。
」卽以大都督趙貴為別道行臺，自蒲阪濟，趣幷州。
遣大都督李賢將精騎一千赴洛陽。
會斌之與斛斯椿爭權不協，斌之遂棄椿還，紿帝云：「高歡兵至。」
七月丁未，帝遂從洛陽率輕騎入關，太祖備儀衛奉迎，謁見東陽驛。
太祖免冠泣涕謝曰：「臣不能式遏寇虐，遂使乘輿遷幸。
請拘司敗，以正刑書。
」帝曰：「公之忠節，曝於朝野。
朕以不德，負乘致寇。
今日相見，深用厚顏。
責在朕躬，無勞謝也。
」乃奉帝都長安。

初，魏帝在洛陽，許以馮翊長公主配太祖，未及結納，而帝西遷。
至是，詔太祖尚之，拜駙馬都尉。
八月，齊神武襲陷潼關，侵華陰。
太祖率諸軍屯霸上以待之。
齊神武留其將薛瑾守關而退。
太祖乃進軍討瑾，虜其卒七千，還長安，進位丞相。
冬十月，齊神武推魏清河王亶子善見為主，徙都於鄴，是為東魏。
十一月，遣儀同李虎與李弼、趙貴等討曹泥於靈州，虎引河灌之。
明年，泥降，遷其豪帥于咸陽。
閏十二月，魏孝武帝崩。
太祖與羣公定策，尊立魏南陽王寶炬為嗣，是為文皇帝。
